items.note: CVDR740897 (Parkeerverordening Zwolle 2026) read in full: 'Geldend van 01-01-2026 t/m heden'; adopted in the council meeting of 16 June 2025; art. 8.2 says it enters into force on 1 January 2026 and the Parkeerverordening 2016 lapses; art. 1.1 defines binnenstad as the area bounded by Stadsgracht, Schuttevaerhaven and Achtergracht; arts 2.1/3.1 cover resident and business permits and garage subscriptions. Title and date match.

Source is the 'Ontwerp-verkeersbesluit wijzigen parkeerverbodszone Hanzeland/Spoorzone' (college, 16 June 2026, to be published 22 June 2026), a DRAFT traffic decision. It does say the council set parking policy on 18 December 2023 (Parkeerstrategie 2040) and elaborated it on 31 March 2025 (Nota parkeren). But it says fiscalised parking 'wordt ingevoerd' only in the district Hanzeland/Spoorzone, not 'in further districts', and the item does not say the document is a draft.
items.corrected_text: The council adopted the Parkeerstrategie 2040 on 18 December 2023 and its elaboration, the Nota parkeren, on 31 March 2025. A draft traffic decision of the college dated 16 June 2026 (to be published on 22 June 2026) cites both dates and says that fiscalised parking (paid parking plus permits on the same spaces) is being introduced in the Hanzeland/Spoorzone district.

items.note: Nota parkeren (annexes dated Jan 2025; adopted 31 March 2025 per the June 2026 documents): six zones, fiscalised parking (paid plus permits) as the starting point (the historic inner city keeps some permit-holder-only spaces until redesign; zones 5 and 6 not worked out), progressive street tariff in zones 1-3 where the hourly rate doubles after one or two hours, garage/hub parking to be cheaper than street parking, phasing 2026-2030 working from the inside out (phase 1 2026-2028, phase 2 2028-2030) all confirmed. However the Nota says of the Schellerbroek parking-disc zone only 'Hier stoppen we in 2026 mee' (a plan, not an accomplished fact).
items.corrected_text: The Nota parkeren (March 2025) splits Zwolle into six zones with fiscalised parking (paid parking plus permits) as the standard, progressive street tariffs in zones 1-3 (the hourly price doubles after one or two hours), and a rule that parking in a garage or hub should be cheaper than on the street. Regulated parking is to be extended step by step from the centre outwards in 2026-2030, and the blue-zone parking disc in part of Schellerbroek is planned to end in 2026.

items.note: Aanwijzingsbesluit gereguleerd parkeren 2026 (Gemeenteblad 2025, 475269, published 7 Nov 2025) read in full: art. 6: zone I Mon-Sat 09:00-23:00 and Sunday 13:00-17:00; zones II and IV Mon-Sat 09:00-20:00 and Sunday 13:00-17:00; art. 6 lid 3: disabled-card exemption does not apply to barrier garages and the Burgemeester Van Roijensingel car park, where payment is due. Decided 4 November 2025; art. 9: in force 1 January 2026. (Zone III has its own hours, not mentioned in the item.)

Regeling parkeervergunningen 2026 (CVDR746264, 'Geldend van 01-01-2026') art. 6: maximum permits are 80% of available spaces in zone I, 85% in zone II (except sector 13, 100%) and 85% in zone IV; art. 8: waiting list; art. 11 lid 2: at most 25 business permits in zone I; art. 12 lid 4: visitor permit 120 hours per quarter. Item wording matches. (In zone I visitor permits only go to residents who held one on 30 April 2025, not mentioned in the item.)

Verordening Parkeerbelastingen Zwolle 2026 (CVDR751055, 'Geldend van 19-12-2025'; adopted in the council meeting of 15 December 2025; levy date 1 January 2026) tariff table: zone I Mon-Sat 9-23h, Sun 13-17h: 4.00 first hour, 8.00 per hour from the second; zone II 2.00 per hour for first two hours then 4.00 from the third; zone IV 1.50 per hour; first resident permit 225 (zone I), 70 (zone II), 50 (zone IV) per year. All match. Stated in force, which is correct as of the ordinance's own dates.

Same tariff table (CVDR751055): Noordereiland garage (zone I) 3.00 per hour, 15.00 per calendar day, lost ticket 42.00; garages Diezerpoort, Emmawijk, Katwolderplein (zone II) and Lübeckplein, Pas de Deux (zone III) 1.50 per hour, 7.50 per day, lost ticket 16.50; several surface car parks (Albert Cuypstraat, Turfmarkt, Schuttevaerkade, Hanzehoven and others; Burgemeester Van Roijensingel is a barrier car park at 1.50/7.50) at 1.50/7.50. All numbers match.

Source is the council document 'Verordening Parkeerbelastingen 2025' (vastgesteld 16 December 2024, in force 1 January 2025) and it still contains placeholders ('datum bekendmaking: xx december 2024', 'voorstel ... van xx-xx-2024'), so it is not the published final text. Zone 1: 3.30 per hour, payment limited to blocks of 60 minutes between 9:00 and 18:00, evening rate 2.20 per hour (maximum 4.40) from 20:00 (Thursday 21:00) to 23:00 are confirmed. For the Noordereiland garage the page gives 'van 9.00 tot 20.00 uur, maximaal 16,50' (a daytime maximum for 09:00-20:00) and 'per kalenderdag (tot 23.00 uur) 20,90'; so '16.50 per day' is wrong as a day rate. The 2026 comparison (4.00/8.00 until 23:00; 15.00 Noordereiland day rate) matches CVDR751055.
items.corrected_text: A council document of 16 December 2024 for the 2025 tariff table (its publication dates still show placeholders, so the final published ordinance may differ) set 3.30 euros per hour in the inner city, with payment limited to blocks of 60 minutes between 09:00 and 18:00, and an evening rate of 2.20 euros per hour (maximum 4.40) from 20:00 (Thursdays 21:00) to 23:00. For the Noordereiland garage it set a maximum of 16.50 euros for 09:00-20:00 and 20.90 euros per calendar day (to 23:00). The 2026 table has a single street tariff of 4.00 euros for the first hour and 8.00 euros per hour after that until 23:00, and a 15.00 euro Noordereiland day rate.

items.note: Nota parkeren annex 3 (tables 3 and 4, 2028): street zone 1 4.50 first hour, 9.00 from the second hour; garages zone 1 3.50 per hour, 17.50 per day; first resident permit 250 (all zone 1) confirmed. The Nota says 'Vanaf 2028 verhogen we alle tarieven stapsgewijs' and 'Vanaf 2026 ... elke twee jaar aangepast op basis van de CPI en eventuele andere omstandigheden' (confirmed). But the Nota only says the 2026 and 2028 tariffs 'worden onderdeel van de Tarievennota 2026 en 2028'; the phrase 'subject to annual confirmation' is not in the cited document (it appears in the separate 16 June 2026 Beslisnota, which says tariffs were set through 2027 subject to annual adoption).
items.corrected_text: The Nota parkeren plans stepwise tariff rises from 2028 (its annex 3 lists them; the 2026 and 2028 tables are to become part of the Tarievennota 2026 and 2028): street parking in zone 1 at 4.50 euros for the first hour and 9.00 euros from the second, garage parking in zone 1 at 3.50 euros per hour and 17.50 euros per day, and a first resident permit of 250 euros. From 2026 all parking tariffs are to be adjusted every two years on the basis of consumer price inflation and other circumstances. These 2028 figures are plans, not tariffs in force.

items.note: Beslisnota voor het college, 'Ontwerpbesluit uitbreiding gereguleerd parkeren 2027', 16 June 2026 (a proposal document: 'Collegebesluit d.d. 16 juni 2026' with Conform/Gewijzigd boxes; extracted text does not show which is ticked; the companion Ontwerp-verkeersbesluit dated 16 June 2026 says the college decided to prepare it under the public procedure). Confirmed: introduction planned for end of Q1 2027 in Hogenkamp/Indische buurt, Spoorzone/Hanzeland, Schellerbroek, Schellerhoek (partly), Wipstrik Zuid (Zuidwest/Zuidoost); end of Schellerbroek parking-disc zone and new disc zone at Forelkolk (about 70 spaces) are DRAFT traffic decisions; 12 meetings, about 3,500 letters, turnout about 8% of households written to. The note says the final decision must be taken in Q3 2026 to allow introduction in Q1 2027; as of 21 October 2026 the item cannot say whether this happened.
items.corrected_text: A college decision note dated 16 June 2026 sets out a draft decision (not yet final) to extend regulated parking, planned for the end of the first quarter of 2027, to Hogenkamp/Indische buurt, Spoorzone/Hanzeland, Schellerbroek, part of Schellerhoek and Wipstrik Zuid. Draft traffic decisions would end the Schellerbroek parking-disc zone and add a parking-disc zone at the Forelkolk shopping-centre car park (about 70 spaces). Twelve residents' meetings drew about 8 percent of the roughly 3,500 households written to. The note says the final decision had to be taken in the third quarter of 2026 for the 2027 start; whether that has happened was not checked.

items.note: Aanwijzingsbesluit gereguleerd parkeren 2026 (Gemeenteblad 2025, 475269) art. 4 table lists exactly 12 facilities with maximum subscriptions: Albert Cuypstraat 28, Assendorperstraat 35, Diezerpoort 305, Dijkstraat (residents) 49, Emmawijk 176, Katwolderplein 350, Q-Park Centrum (residents and businesses) 165, Burgemeester Van Roijensingel 184, Schuttevaerkade 70, Turfmarkt 177, Van der Laenstraat 64, Van Karnebeekstraat P2 21. The examples quoted match. 'Privately run' for Q-Park Centrum is confirmed by Q-Park's own pages and the Nota (private garage).

RDW NPR open data (index https://npropendata.rdw.nl/parkingdata/v2 plus the per-facility static and dynamic records, fetched 21 October 2026): operator 'Zwolle' with capacities Katwolderplein 700, Diezerpoort 611, Noordereiland Dek 330 and Kelder 340, Lübeckplein 385, Pas de Deux 204, Burgemeester Van Roijensingel 190 (a surface car park, not a garage). Live records have lastUpdated 24 June 2025 (Hanzeland) and 7 July 2025 (the rest), so 'June-July 2025' is right. Caveats: the cited URL is only the index; the live capacities differ from the static ones (e.g. Diezerpoort 562, Katwolderplein 679); 'appear not to be maintained' is an inference. Note also that the Q-Park P+R record IS fresh (see item 12).

Q-Park Zwolle overview page (read 21 October 2026) lists Centrum (Pletterstraat 41), Maagjesbolwerk (Maagjesbolwerk 54) and P+R Zwolle (Hanzelaan 101) and says 'vanaf 20 per dag' at Maagjesbolwerk and 'vanaf 12 per dag' at the P+R, with discount for OV-chipkaart/NS-Business Card holders and online reservation. But: (a) capacities 323 (Centrum) and 453 (Maagjesbolwerk) and the same-day domestic train condition are on the sub-pages, not the cited URL; (b) the same page is inconsistent on prices: page title 'Reserveren vanaf 18 per dag' and a deal 'vanaf 16,50 per dag' next to the 20 and 12; (c) all facility tariff tables show 'De tarieven konden helaas niet geladen worden', so these are advertised 'from' prices, not a verified tariff; (d) the P+R page says 207 spaces (and 2 disabled), while the RDW live record (ZWOLLE-P+R Zwolle, updated 21 Oct 2026) says capacity 132 with 31 vacant, and the RDW static record gives no capacity; our feed has 132. Not reconciled.
items.corrected_text: Q-Park lists three facilities in Zwolle: the garage Centrum at Pletterstraat 41 (323 spaces), the garage Maagjesbolwerk at Maagjesbolwerk 54 (453 spaces) and the P+R at Hanzelaan 101 near the station (207 spaces on Q-Park's own page; the open-data live record gives a capacity of 132, and the two were not reconciled). Its Zwolle page, read on 21 October 2026, advertises 'from' prices of 20 euros per day at Maagjesbolwerk and 12 euros per day at the P+R, but the same page also shows a deal from 16.50 euros per day and a page title 'from 18 euros per day', and the facility tariff tables did not load, so these are advertised starting prices rather than a verified tariff. A rail-traveller discount applies to domestic train journeys under conditions on the P+R page, and online reservation is offered.

items.note: Q-Park Centrum page (read 21 Oct 2026): 20 electric charge points; Q-Park Maagjesbolwerk page: 26; RDW static record for Parkeergarage Katwoldeplein lists chargingPointCapacity 30. Nota parkeren section 6.4: over 1,100 public charge points in the municipality, about fifty in its accommodations; at least a hundred more to be added in current accommodations; new area developments must have working charge points at at least 20% of spaces on completion; street-charging concession runs to 01-07-2027. All match. Cited URL covers only the Q-Park Centrum part; the 1,100 figure is from early 2025.

Nota parkeren section 6.1-6.3: about 2.5 million parking transactions in 2023, 57% of street transactions via phone app (belparkeren), 93% of permit requests via the digital counter, enforcement scan car with more than 1 million scans, barrier garages keep cash payment for now with app payment and reservation to be introduced. All match; figures are from 2023/early 2025.

Raadsvoorstel 'Mobiliteitshub Weezenlanden-Noord: Ontwerp, kredietaanpassing en wijziging omgevingsplan' (12 November 2025): first centre hub; under Luttenbergstraat and the front garden of the Provinciehuis; shrunk by 24 places from 450 to 426; extra credit of 7.2 million requested (total 52.6 million vs 45.4); charging 2.5% (11 points) at opening instead of 20% because of grid congestion; planned start of construction mid-2027 and expected delivery in 2030. All as stated and worded as a proposal/expectation. Caveats: the council decision on the credit (December 2025) and a pending court case on tree felling were not checked, so the 2030 date is still only a plan.

Raadsbrief 'Locatiebesluit Tijdelijke Parkeervoorziening Weezenlanden-Noord' dated 6 May 2025 reports a 'principebesluit' (decision in principle, no decision date given): temporary parking at the Goertjesweg (an existing car park with room for 80 places, rented from the owner; only an oral agreement, rent EUR 34,500 per year, contract not final; meant for provincial staff), Turfmarkt for residents of Weezenlanden-Noord, 20 extra visitor places on the Schuurmanstraat. 400 spaces needed in and around the district and part of the provincial car park closes: confirmed. 'College decided in May 2025' is too exact and the decision is only in principle.
items.corrected_text: A council letter of 6 May 2025 reported that the college had decided in principle to provide temporary parking while the Weezenlanden-Noord hub is built: a site on the Goertjesweg (an existing car park with room for about 80 places, to be rented, with the lease not yet final), resident parking at the Turfmarkt and 20 extra visitor places on the Schuurmanstraat. The study put the need at 400 spaces in and around the district, and part of the provincial car park closes during construction.

items.note: Beslisnota voor de raad 'Mobiliteitshubs Nieuwe Veemarkt en parkeren' (3 October 2023, final version 1.0): proposal to make a credit of 28,500,000 euros available; hub in the east on the inner-city side of about 225 places and hub in the west along the A28 of about 300 places (hub and deck); about 950 parking places in the plan overall; compensation of 100 places guaranteed for the existing Emmadek. Worded as a request, which is right. Caveat: three years old, the council outcome and any later change to the numbers were not checked.

corrected_summary: Zwolle runs a zoned, tax-based parking system. The Parkeerverordening Zwolle 2026 (adopted by the council on 16 June 2025, in force since 1 January 2026) and the Verordening Parkeerbelastingen Zwolle 2026 (adopted 15 December 2025) set the rules and prices. In the inner city, street parking is paid Monday to Saturday from 09:00 to 23:00 (Sundays 13:00 to 17:00) and costs 4.00 euros for the first hour and 8.00 euros per hour after that, while municipal garages in the ring around the centre and near the station charge 1.50 euros per hour (7.50 euros per day) and the Noordereiland garage in the inner city 3.00 euros per hour (15.00 euros per day). Policy rests on the Parkeerstrategie 2040 (council, 18 December 2023) and the Nota parkeren (council, 31 March 2025): residents' permits are capped (80 to 85 percent of the permit-eligible spaces in most zones), garages are meant to be cheaper than streets, and the Nota plans stepwise tariff increases from 2028 and a step-by-step extension of regulated parking over 2026 to 2030. A draft college decision of 16 June 2026 proposes extending regulated parking to further districts at the end of the first quarter of 2027; the final decision was due in the third quarter of 2026 and its status was not checked. The city owns and runs most large garages (Katwolderplein, Diezerpoort, Noordereiland, Lübeckplein, Pas de Deux, Emmawijk), while Q-Park operates Centrum (323 spaces), Maagjesbolwerk (453) and the P+R at Hanzelaan 101 near the station, whose capacity is 207 on Q-Park's page but 132 in the open-data record; Q-Park's 'from 12 euros per day' and 'from 20 euros per day' prices are advertised starting prices, not a verified tariff. The first new centre mobility hub, Weezenlanden-Noord (426 spaces, underground), is expected to open in 2030 according to a November 2025 council proposal that asked for 7.2 million euros of extra credit, with temporary parking arranged elsewhere in the meantime; in 2023 the college proposed 28.5 million euros for the Nieuwe Veemarkt hubs (about 950 places in the plan). The municipal open-data live feeds for the city garages were last updated in June and July 2025, although the Q-Park P+R record was current on 21 October 2026, and no published utilisation statistics were found. The municipal website zwolle.nl was unavailable (HTTP 429) and was not used.
